'''Daniel L. Goroff''' is an American [[mathematician]] and [[Academic administration|academic administrator]]. He is currently the Vice President and Program Director at the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]], where he manages programs centered on [[economics]] and the quality of [[Postgraduate education|graduate education]].<ref name="SloanBio">{{cite web |title=Daniel L. Goroff - Program Director |url=https://sloan.org/about/staff/daniel-l-goroff |website=sloan.org |publisher=Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |access-date=2024-05-22}}</ref> He was a [[technology policy]] official in the [[Joe Biden|Biden]] [[White House]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=About {{!}} Alfred P. Sloan Foundation |url=https://sloan.org/about/staff/daniel-l-goroff |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=sloan.org |language=en}}</ref> 

==Education==
Goroff received his B.A. and M.A. degrees from [[Harvard University]]. He then attended the [[University of Cambridge]] as a Churchill Scholar, earning an M.Phil. He completed his Ph.D. in mathematics at [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[Fields Medal]]ist [[William Thurston]].<ref name="MathGenealogy">{{cite web |title=Daniel Lewis Goroff |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=12853 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=2024-05-22}}</ref>

==Career==
Goroff spent over twenty years at [[Harvard University]] as a Professor of the Practice of Mathematics and Associate Dean of Harvard College. He later served as the Vice President for Academic Affairs and Dean of the Faculty at [[Harvey Mudd College]].<ref name="HMC">{{cite web |title=Former Dean of Faculty Daniel Goroff Returns to Sloan Foundation |url=https://www.hmc.edu/about/news/ |website=hmc.edu |publisher=Harvey Mudd College |access-date=2024-05-22}}</ref>

In the public sector, Goroff has twice worked at the [[White House Office of Science and Technology Policy]] (OSTP), most recently as Deputy Director for Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences.<ref name="OSTP">{{cite web |title=OSTP Leadership |url=https://www.whitehouse.gov/ostp/ |website=whitehouse.gov |access-date=2024-05-22}}</ref>

==Research and publications==
His research focuses on [[celestial mechanics]] and [[dynamical systems]]. He is particularly noted for his work on the history of mathematics, including his extensive editing and translation of [[Henri Poincaré]]'s ''Les Méthodes Nouvelles de la Mécanique Céleste''.
